title: Minimum Right Shifts to Sort the Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of distinct positive integers, determine the least number of right shifts needed to sort the array, or return -1 if sorting is impossible.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of distinct positive integers, determine the least number of right shifts needed to sort the array, or return -1 if sorting is impossible. A right shift moves each element to the next index, wrapping around to the start.
constraints: A right shift removes the last element and inserts it at the front.
Return the minimum number of right shifts needed to make nums nondecreasing.
Return -1 if no rotation of nums is nondecreasing.
reference_solution:
def minimum_right_shifts_to_sort(nums):
    drops=[i for i in range(len(nums)) if nums[i]>nums[(i+1)%len(nums)]]
    if not drops:return 0
    if len(drops)>1:return -1
    shift=len(nums)-1-drops[0]
    return shift

def minimum_right_shifts_to_sort(nums):
    drops=[i for i in range(len(nums)) if nums[i]>nums[(i+1)%len(nums)]]
    if not drops:return 0
    if len(drops)>1:return -1
    shift=drops[0]+1

hints: A sorted circular rotation has at most one adjacent descent around the circle.
Find indices whose value is greater than the next circular value.
No drops means already sorted; one drop determines how many suffix values must move to the front; more than one is impossible.
Rotating immediately after the unique drop places the global low segment before the high segment, and all internal pairs are already ordered.
